newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end a record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end a record high.

text.p: Soaring pharmaceutical stock prices lifted Swiss share indices by more than one percent to a record close.
The U.S. employment cost index released today, which was below market expectations, and the firming U.S. dollar also gave shares a boost, share dealers said.

The blue-chip Swiss Market Index ended 55.0 points, or 1.33 percent, higher at 4,182.9 after hitting an intraday high of 4,182.9. The broad Swiss Performance Index gained 34.16 points, or 1.29 percent, to end at 2,676.67.

Most-active Roche certificates, which have been in the limelight during the past few sessions due to varied speculation about mergers or spin-offs, jumped 230 francs, or nearly two percent, to 12,010. One dealer said rumours that the company may launch a new drug also helped trigger the rise.
Novartis registered shares rose 28 francs to 1,614. The company said 1996 group sales totalled 36.23 billion francs after 35.94 billion in 1995. The group also said it expected a flat 1996 profit.
Nestle, ABB, Holderbank, Surveillance and SMH were other clear winners in the blue-chip segment.
UBS and Winterthur firmed more than one percent.
Swissair continued its recent solid performance, climbing 34 francs, or 2.76 percent, to 1,267.
Sulzer, Clariant and Swiss Re were among the few blue chips to post losses.
